purpose: Resolve the finite-characteristic loopholes in the v4.2 topology-changed OR2+XOR3 common-basis barrier. The characteristic-zero proof exposes a factor 7, and characteristic two also requires separate treatment. Prove that characteristic 7 genuinely admits OR2+XOR3 parity bases, classify them exactly, and then show that the dual EQ3 fanout tensor necessarily mixes parity. Together with the characteristic-two hyperdeterminant barrier, this closes the one-common-basis local matchgate route over every field.

setup.variable_basis: S=T^(-T), up to an irrelevant common nonzero scalar.
setup.necessary_condition: Every local matchgate signature has pure Hamming parity.

generic_characteristic.result: For characteristic different from 2 and 7, the v4.2 case split applies verbatim: OR2 odd parity forces XOR3 to mix parity; OR2 even combined with XOR3 even or odd yields respectively 7*C^2=0 or 7*A^2=0 with the relevant variable nonzero. Hence no invertible common basis exists.
generic_characteristic.note: Characteristic 3 is included: the intermediate equations only strengthen to a zero diagonal entry and do not produce an invertible exception.

characteristic_7_classification.theorem: Over any field of characteristic 7, the invertible T making both OR2 and XOR3 pure parity fall into exactly two families.
derivation: In the OR2-even/XOR3-even branch, v4.2 gives D^2=-3C^2=4C^2, so D=+/-2C. The D=-2C branch makes Delta zero after the OR2 equation; D=2C forces A=2B and is invertible.
In the OR2-even/XOR3-odd branch, B^2=-3A^2=4A^2, so B=+/-2A. The B=-2A branch makes Delta zero; B=2A forces C=2D and is invertible.
The OR2-odd branch remains impossible because characteristic 7 is not characteristic 2.
characteristic_7_classification.prime_field_count_control: Over GF(7), each family has 6*6=36 matrices and the families are disjoint, giving exactly 72 invertible OR2+XOR3 parity bases. The checker exhausts all 7^4 matrices and confirms this count.

eq3_obstruction_in_characteristic_7.dual_weights: Ignoring the common Delta^(-3) scalar, for S=T^(-T) the transformed EQ3 Hamming-weight amplitudes are e0=D^3-C^3, e1=-B*D^2+A*C^2, e2=D*B^2-C*A^2, e3=A^3-B^3.
eq3_obstruction_in_characteristic_7.family_EE: With A=2B and D=2C in characteristic 7: e0=e3=0, e1=-2*B*C^2 !=0, e2=-2*C*B^2 !=0.
eq3_obstruction_in_characteristic_7.conclusion: In both exceptional families EQ3 has nonzero weight-1 and weight-2 amplitudes simultaneously. Therefore its support meets odd and even Hamming parity and it is not a matchgate signature.

characteristic_2.result: The v3.9 Cayley-hyperdeterminant theorem already proves something stronger: EQ3 cannot be taken to pure parity by any invertible independent local gauges at all in characteristic two. Hence a common basis is impossible a fortiori.

main_theorem.name: NO_FIELD_ADMITS_ONE_COMMON_BASIS_FOR_EQ3_OR2_XOR3_MATCHGATE_PARITY
main_theorem.statement: Over every field, there is no invertible 2x2 common holographic basis whose variable-side transform makes EQ3 pure parity and whose dual constraint-side transform makes both OR2 and XOR3 pure parity.
main_theorem.scope: This closes the one-common-basis local matchgate route for the v4.1 topology-changed carrier. It does not rule out genuinely nonlocal Gaussianization, topology changes that eliminate equality fanout before local conversion, or non-matchgate algorithms.

next_target.name: E8_NONLOCAL_EQUALITY_FANOUT_ELIMINATION_OR_COMPRESSED_GLOBAL_INVARIANT_V4_6
next_target.directive: All characteristics are now closed for local common-basis conversion. Any surviving finite-field/Pfaffian route must eliminate or couple EQ3 fanout nonlocally before Gaussianization. In parallel, the Macaulay route must compress unbounded-degree information rather than enumerate monomials. Require polynomial state, exact zero-test and polynomial witness reconstruction.
